title: Best free AI lip sync tools (2026): limits & watermarks
summary: Find a free lip sync workflow for video or a portrait. Compare no-signup trials, duration limits, watermarks, local software, and when paying helps.
body_markdown:
## Quick answer


**Start with**


[Magic Hour Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) **for a free browser trial using your own face video and audio: three guest attempts per day, up to ten seconds each, with a watermark.**


For a still portrait, use[Talking Photo](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-talking-photo) instead. Free generation, watermark-free downloading, and commercial permission are three different conditions.


Magic Hour publishes this guide and is included. We selected tools with a current usable free route and a distinct fit for video, portraits, or local operation, then compared documented inputs, limits, watermarks, and availability. This is not a controlled output-quality benchmark; sources were checked September 13, 2026.

### Lip-sync your own clip


Upload a video and audio track to Magic Hour, generate a short sample, and check timing around consonants and head turns.


[Try Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync)


## 1. Magic Hour: try your own footage without signup


Upload a short video with one clear face and a separate audio recording. A front-facing clip with little camera movement makes a useful first attempt. Include a pause so you can see whether the mouth closes when the speaker stops.


For a simple trial, say: “Hello, Maya. Your preview is ready.” Record it clearly and keep it within the ten-second limit. Use your own footage or media you have permission to edit. Open[Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) , add both files, generate, and inspect the complete video.


Free results carry a watermark. If the sample fits your project, compare the[paid plans](https://magichour.ai/pricing) for longer work, credit usage, watermark-free video, and commercial use. Do not purchase a longer run to fix a face that is already distorted in the short one; change the input first.


## 2. Talking Photo: use a portrait directly


The[Talking Photo tool](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-talking-photo) starts from a still image and audio. Its current FAQ states three guest attempts per day and a five-second free clip limit. Record a short line such as “Welcome back. Let's get started,” rather than squeezing a paragraph into the sample.


Choose a clear portrait with one visible face and space around the chin. Start with a natural expression and unobstructed eyes and mouth. Watch for moving teeth, changing face shape, and a jaw that keeps moving during silence.


A talking photo exports a video. It does not inherit the watermark-free policy of Magic Hour's free still-image tools. For a detailed shortlist, read[best AI talking-photo tools](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-talking-photo-tools-2026) .


## 3. HeyGen: evaluate a presenter workflow


[HeyGen’s browser pricing page](https://www.heygen.com/pricing) lists three free videos per month, each up to one minute. Its[mobile free-plan guide](https://help.heygen.com/en/articles/10207693-how-to-get-started-with-heygen-for-mobile) separately lists a regional allowance of one to three free videos and a 720p sharing link. These are different surfaces: confirm the quota and download options in the account you will use. Creator includes 1080p export and watermark removal. Browser and mobile details were rechecked October 10, 2026.


Use this route when your main task is building a presenter video from a script. Before generating the full message, check the available avatar, voice pronunciation, and export settings.


## 4. LatentSync 1.6: run video lip sync locally


[ByteDance LatentSync](https://github.com/bytedance/LatentSync) takes an existing video and replacement audio, then generates synchronized mouth motion locally. Version 1.6 uses 512-by-512 face-region training and the project is licensed under Apache 2.0. It is a video lip-sync workflow rather than a still-photo animator.


Choose it when local operation and code-level control justify setup work. The current inference path targets CUDA, so verify your environment before committing to it. Review the[1.6 changelog](https://github.com/bytedance/LatentSync/blob/main/docs/changelog_v1.6.md) , model files, face coverage and full output; an open-source license does not guarantee that every input or output is suitable for commercial use.

## Make the first attempt count


1. Choose one visible speaker and trim a short, continuous shot.
2. Record one clear line. Avoid overlapping speakers and loud background music.
3. Match the clip and audio lengths as closely as practical.
4. Generate once and watch the downloaded result with sound.
5. If it fails, change the source or the specific problem before spending the next attempt.


For a walkthrough with upload screenshots, see[how to lip sync a video](https://magichour.ai/blog/how-to-lip-sync-a-video-with-ai) .


## Why a lip-sync clip ends early—or does not move


**The shorter selected segment sets the output length.** In the signed-in editor, check both video and audio trim handles. An eight-second video selection paired with six seconds of audio produces a six-second selection; this is an illustrative timing calculation, not a measured output. Move the audio selection if the clip starts at the wrong word.


**Standard and Pro need visible source mouth movement.** A frozen face or a still portrait is not a useful test for those modes. Use[Talking Photo](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-talking-photo) for a portrait. Lip Sync changes mouth movement to follow finished audio; it does not translate the words, create a song from lyrics, or retime the entire performance.


The[current Lip Sync guide](https://help.magichour.ai/en/articles/15011107) separates the no-signup route from[the full Lip Sync editor](https://magichour.ai/create/lip-sync) . The guest tool accepts uploaded or preset video and audio, with 576px output. Create requires sign-in and generation credits; it also accepts YouTube video and offers mode and trim controls. Confirm its estimate and available settings before generating.


If a result is silent or cut short, inspect the downloaded file and the selected audio section before repeating the job. Keep the project ID and the timestamp where the problem occurs for support review. Repeating an unchanged request is not a timing fix.


## When a paid plan is worth considering


Upgrade when the sample is already usable and your project needs more duration, more attempts, the paid mode, or a qualifying export. A paid tier is not evidence of better results on every input.


For a client deliverable, approve one representative sample before generating every language or version. Keep the script, face source, and voice permissions with the project. See the[full lip sync comparison](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-lip-sync-tools) for subscription and usage-cost examples.


## From one free trial to three language versions


**Approve one short version before paying for a multilingual batch.** Start with a six-second, single-speaker video and audio of similar length. Include a pause and a complete final word. One practice line is “Please bring my blue bag. Maya will pick it up tomorrow.” Time your recording; shorten the sentence if it exceeds the selected duration.


Lip Sync uses your existing video and replacement audio. Prepare translations and narration first; the upload workflow does not automatically translate the script or clone a voice. If you need speech from text, prepare and review it in[AI Voice Generator](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-voice-generator) before importing the audio. Confirm permission for the face and voice, and have a fluent speaker check each translated recording.


**Budget generated seconds, including planned retries.** Three language versions × six seconds × two planned attempts = 36 generated seconds. That is a planning example, not an observed success rate or a vendor price. Check the quote for the selected mode and settings; include rejected attempts in the project budget rather than dividing cost by only the final edit’s duration.


The six-second first test fits Magic Hour’s documented ten-second guest limit. Free video carries a watermark. If the result meets your acceptance criteria, check[current plans and credit packs](https://magichour.ai/pricing) for watermark-free video; a subscription’s additional features are separate from buying generation credits.


Run the representative sample in[Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) , download it, and check mouth closure, pauses, identity and the final word. Approve that version before processing the other languages. Review each finished translation independently: a good first result does not prove the timing or meaning of the next recording.


## A lip-sync test that exposes real limits


**Direct answer:** A free lip-sync tool is useful only when the downloaded clip preserves speech timing, identity and resolution. Judge the full sentence, not a silent preview or one mouth shape.


**Test material.** Use a clip no longer than ten seconds containing closed-mouth sounds, wide vowels, teeth visibility and a short pause. Include one front-facing speaker and one mild profile turn. Keep the same audio and source video across tools.


**Review criteria.** Check mouth closure, jaw motion, teeth, tongue artifacts, facial drift, head movement, audio offset and recovery after pauses. Record free-duration limits, watermark, queue, retries and commercial-use terms.


**Upgrade rule.** Pay when a tool passes your hardest phonemes and the paid tier clearly removes a verified constraint such as duration, resolution, watermark, queue time or API access.


**Try the workflow:**[Open the matching Magic Hour tool](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) . Use the same representative input and acceptance criteria before comparing results.
